- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match true mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and forecast is below recent 10-day average, model underestimates upward momentum; raise forecast by 2–5% to reflect sentiment-driven bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4); apply +1–3% bias to first 5 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is flat or near-zero, model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match true price momentum.
- If forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction by 2–5% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
